chunks: Al-Dhahabi said in his Mizan, vol. 3, p. 129:
Abu Abd Allah ibn al-Mu'allim the Rafidi, surnamed Sheikh al-Mufid — he has many compilations; he died in the year 413, and he was possessed of greatness and grandeur in the Buyid state.

Sheikh al-Mufid, the scholar of the Rafida — Abu Abd Allah ibn al-Mu'allim, possessor of compilations... numbering two hundred works... He wielded great power by virtue of 'Adud al-Dawla. Eighty thousand Rafidis escorted his funeral. He died in the year 413.
ai.seo_question: What did the Sunni scholar al-Dhahabi write about Sheikh al-Mufid in Mizan al-I'tidal?
ai.summary: Al-Dhahabi records in his Mizan al-I'tidal (vol. 3, pp. 129 and 131) two biographical entries on Sheikh al-Mufid (d. 413 AH), the foremost Shia theologian and jurist of his era. Despite his polemical use of the term 'Rafidi,' al-Dhahabi — an adversarial Sunni critic — nonetheless attests to al-Mufid's immense scholarly output (~200 works), his commanding prestige under the Buyid dynasty through 'Adud al-Dawla, and that eighty thousand mourners accompanied his funeral procession; this entry appears here as unsolicited testimony from an opponent underscoring al-Mufid's extraordinary stature.
